name: Tatum White
strengths: White explodes off the snap with forward lean for a 290-lb freshman — beat the center's hands clean on multiple interior clips.
White punches and sheds: violent two-hand strike at 3-tech lifts the guard's pads and clears a path for TFL pursuit.
White absorbs double teams and holds the point without walking backward — goal-line snaps show him clogging the A-gap and forcing bounce.
White's motor shows on backside pursuit 15–20 yards downfield; length also gets into throwing lanes when he plays over the ball.
weaknesses: White rises out of his stance too early on some snaps — guards get under him when pad level climbs.
White is mostly one-speed bull/push as a freshman — needs rip/swim/push-pull counters as a pass rusher.
White can lunge and overrun gaps chasing splash plays, opening cutback lanes.
comparison: White comps to Christian Barmore — 6-4/6-5 interior mold with length, violent hands, and early disruptive juice who grows into an every-down presence.
projection: White projects as a Year 2–3 SEC rotation interior DL (develop Year 1). Ceiling: every-down 3-tech / hybrid starter — the long Heard County freshman who already holds doubles and finishes TFLs.
schemeFit: White fits as a 3-tech / 4i who can two-gap on early downs and push the pocket inside on obvious pass.
insiderNotes: White's freshman Hudl (1:54 package) shows real interior tools at 6-5 / 290: get-off, hand violence, double-team anchor, and pursuit motor. Pass-rush counters and pad-level consistency are the growth items. Florida offered Sept 1, 2026.
staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-09-01 from Hudl embed https://www.hudl.com/embed/video/3/26746762/68ee7956ef5f0b59df40527c (Freshman Year package, ~1:54). filmWatched:true. Comp size-matched within ~1-2 inches (Barmore) — not a Florida-alum default.
recruitingStory: Tatum White is a 4-star 2029 DL · listed 6-5 / 290 · Heard County (Franklin, GA) · Florida offered Sept 1, 2026 · uncommitted.
angle: Lead with freshman interior tape — get-off, hand violence, doubles anchor — then Florida offer stake.
